sourceInformation.perspective: Fixed oblique overhead 3D cutaway; player-follow framing on narrow screens
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js 0.180.0 WebGPURenderer / WebGPU with WebGL2 fallback; TSL; Rapier 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio; AI Hub session client 1.4.0; WebRTC; BroadcastChannel. Engine and WASM embedded.
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural stylized cel shading, ink outlines, midnight teal and warm parchment
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer with authored keyframe clips; procedural scene effects
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated minor music-box waltz at 10% default volume, synthesized effects and Animalese-style gibberish voices; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: 1–2 cooperative shared-world AI Hub sessions; standalone same-browser tab rooms and manual remote WebRTC invitations. Direct peer connectivity required; no TURN relay.
sourceInformation.testing: 154 checks passed: full campaign, WebGPU renderer health, collisions, emulated standard gamepad, touch/rotation, 14 offline sound renders, real co-op/WebRTC, and four AI Hub harness scenarios. Screenshots used for visual review. Physical-controller and real-phone results: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: none for source research; native model knowledge only. Read only the supplied AI Hub integration specification/client; no internet searches.

testingFeedback: 8 issues caught: 5 by automated checks, including offline-audio initialization and initial Hub guest traffic, and 3 by visual review. All were fixed.
1 critical gameplay issue: a frame-loop variable scope error stopped play. It was fixed; the separate Hub startup conformance issue was also fixed.
The scripted full campaign: key pickup, locked chambers, all three fragments, persistent floor transitions, and the final escape.
Headless WebGPU screenshots were blank and could not judge artwork; renderer-state checks and WebGL2 screenshots were more useful.
engineFeedback: Three.js TSL made stepped cel shading reusable, and AnimationMixer provided a reliable base for the character loops.
Headless WebGPU initially lost its device. A minimal cube isolated the launch configuration; explicit ANGLE/SwiftShader plus Vulkan flags fixed it.
The exploration state, one-tool inventory, controller menus, procedural environment, synthesized audio, and host-authoritative co-op.
Distinguishing an actual GPU device failure from the separate headless canvas screenshot limitation.
Provide clearer device-loss diagnostics and a reliable built-in screenshot/readback path.
promptFeedback: The source, visual direction, single-file deliverable, and controller-first requirements set a clear creative target.
The research ban and mandatory external integration URL needed to be interpreted together.
Completing gameplay, procedural art/audio, controller and touch UX, and several multiplayer paths as one polished standalone file.
Explicitly exempt required integration documentation from the research ban and distinguish local-tab and remote multiplayer requirements.

aiHub.name: Urn Welcome
aiHub.description: Explore a crooked midnight mansion, coax open locked doors, and recover three fragments of a family urn. Keep your match alight and your nerve intact, alone or with a fellow intruder.
aiHub.controls: Move: WASD / arrows / left stick; interact: E / Cross; relight or flash: Space / Square; drop: Q / Triangle; map: M / Touchpad; pause: Esc / Options; touch: drag to move, contextual action.
